notes:
Summary: Aldergate is a regional logistics platform (fleet routing + customer support) evaluating Redwood Dedicated with optional Private control plane. Primary driver: predictable throughput for real-time reranking and embedding refresh windows.

Throughput negotiation specifics (customer <-> Redwood positions):
- Customer asks: min guaranteed throughput = 150k tokens/sec sustained during business hours (8a-8p PST). Concurrency target = 40 concurrent requests for routing service. Burst policy requested: up to 2x sustained throughput (300k tokens/sec) for 10 minutes with soft throttling thereafter.
- Redwood draft: propose min guarantee = 120k tokens/sec sustained; concurrency cap = 50 concurrent lightweight requests or 30 heavy requests (depends on avg token length). Burst policy: 2x for 5 minutes, then prioritized queueing; documented cost for sustained bursts.
- Technical basis: benchmarked redwood-ev1-large / quantized variant: ~15k tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU at 2048 context for reranking model. Sizing note: 8 GPUs yields ~120k sustained; 10 GPUs required to hit customer 150k margin with headroom for KV cache pressure.

Latency / SLO discussion:
- Customer target: p95 generation latency < 200ms for routing micro-inferences, p99 < 350ms. Must maintain while meeting throughput guarantees.
- Redwood asks to accept latency SLO scoped to model variant and request size; fallbacks allowed to quantized model with slightly higher latency but cost savings.

Reserved GPU planning & pricing:
- Two options on table: 1) Reserved pool (8-10 GPUs committed) + burst capacity on shared cluster (pay-as-you-burst). 2) Fully reserved (10 GPUs) for hard guarantees; higher ARR discount.
- Customer sensitive to unit cost: wants blended per-token price with ramp discounts tied to committed tokens/sec. Interested in Optimize tool suggestions for batching and KV caching to reduce required GPU count.

SLA negotiation points (open):
- Definition of "throughput breach" (5 consecutive minutes below min tokens/sec vs 30-minute window)
